heroHeadline: National Total Passes 5,248 Fires and 4.49M Hectares as BC Downgrades Pear Lake and Ainslie Creek from 'Wildfire of Note'
heroSubtitle: Canada's season-to-date total reached 5,248 fires and 4,492,283 hectares burned as of August 31, led by the Northwest Territories (1.69M ha), Quebec, Ontario and British Columbia. In BC, the Pear Lake fire (166,132 ha) and the Ainslie Creek/Brunswick Creek complex near Merritt lost their 'wildfire of note' status on September 3 as growth stalled and perimeters became secure, while the Bald Range fire near Summerland had its area restriction order rescinded September 4 as activity decreased. Northwestern Ontario's active fire count climbed to 62 after nine small new starts over September 2–3, though the Rinker Lake Complex (Thunder Bay 36, Dryden 34, Dryden 35 — 377,240 hectares combined) remains not under control with activity on the low end. No new deaths or evacuation orders were identified this cycle.
footerNote: Data sourced from official reports, major outlets, and institutional analyses.
